# MILESTONE 2 
In this document, I will clean, test, and explore Table 98-10-0458-01 
[@MainModeofCommuting] from the 2021 Canadian Census with the following research 
question in mind: Do Canadian men and women choose different commuting modes and 
if so, does this gender difference vary by province/territory?

# Data Cleaning 

```{r}
#| message: false

# install.packages(tidyverse)
# install.packages("dplyr")
# install.packages("knitr")
# install.packages("tinytable")
# install.packages("readr")
# install.packages("ggrepel")

library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(tinytable)
library(readr)
library(ggrepel)
```

```{r}
# Read in raw data 

#| echo: false
raw_data <- read.csv("Commute_Data_Database.csv")
```

```{r}
# Renaming columns that will not be filtered out to remove periods and numbers 
# (Geography, Gender, Mode, Immigrant_Status, and Count)

commute_relabeled_cols <- raw_data |>
  rename(
    Geography = GEO, 
    Gender = Gender..3., 
    Mode = Main.mode.of.commuting..11A., 
    Immigrant_Status = Immigrant.status.and.period.of.immigration..11., 
    Count = VALUE
  )

names(commute_relabeled_cols) # Confirming renaming worked as planned
```
```{r}
# Setting which modes of transportation will be kept in this dataset 
# Filtering out "Driver with 1 or more workers", "Passenger with 2 or more
# workers", and "Sustainable transportation" as these include overlap with 
# "Car, truck, or van", "Public transit", "Active transportation", and "Other"
# (the transportation modes that I am keeping in the cleaned dataset)

modes_keep <- c("Car, truck or van", "Public transit", "Active transportation", 
                "Other method")

# Filtering out unnecessary columns and ensuring that the "Immigrant 
# Status" column does not include duplicates in overlapping categories by only 
# looking at "Total - Immigrant status and period of immigration"

commute_clean <- commute_relabeled_cols |> 
  filter(
    Immigrant_Status == "Total - Immigrant status and period of immigration", 
    Mode %in% modes_keep
  ) |> 
  select(Geography, Gender, Mode, Count)

# Test to ensure that filtered output has the number of rows (Should be 13 
# provinces x 2 genders x 4 modes of transportation)
stopifnot(nrow(commute_clean) == 104) 
```

```{r}
# Testing if Count column is the correct class (should be an integer)

stopifnot(is.integer(commute_clean$Count))
```

```{r}
# Arranging by Geography, then Gender, then Mode to allow for easy viewing and 
# comparison of rows

commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  arrange(Geography, Gender, Mode)

commute_clean
```

```{r}
# Adding a "Total" column to allow percentage calculation for each row of the 
# data frame 

commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  group_by(Geography, Gender) |> 
  mutate(Total = sum(Count)) |> 
  ungroup()

commute_clean
```

```{r}
# Adding a "Percent" column to match with simulated data visualization and 
# plan for EDA

commute_clean <- commute_clean |> 
  mutate(Percent = Count / Total * 100)

commute_clean
```
```{r}
# Testing if Total and Percent columns are the correct class (Total should be 
# an integer column and Percent should be a double format)

stopifnot(is.integer(commute_clean$Total))
stopifnot(is.double(commute_clean$Percent))
```

```{r}
# Creating table from commute_clean for easy viewing

commute_clean |> 
  tt() |> 
  format_tt(j = c("Count", "Total"), digits = 0, num_fmt = "decimal", 
            num_mark_big = ",") |>
  format_tt(j = "Percent", fn = \(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", x)) |>
  style_tt(j = 1:6, align = "lllrrr")
```

```{r}
# Test to ensure "Count" does not include negative values
stopifnot(
  "Count has negative values"       = all(commute_clean$Count >= 0)
)

# Test to ensure there are no missing values in dataset
stopifnot("Data contains missing values" = !anyNA(commute_clean))

# Test to ensure there is no blank text strings in dataset
stopifnot(
  "Blank text found" = all(
    commute_clean |> 
      select(where(is.character)) |> 
      map_lgl(\(x) all(str_trim(x) !=""))
  )
)
```

```{r}
# Writing new cleaned data CSV file

write_csv(commute_clean, "Cleaned_Commute.csv")
```

```{r}
# A final test to ensure that all columns (Mode, Gender, and Geography) align 
# with expected n and include the expected content 

mode_counts   <- count(commute_clean, Mode)
gender_counts <- count(commute_clean, Gender)
geography_counts <- count(commute_clean, Geography)

stopifnot(
  nrow(mode_counts) == 4,     # Expected exactly 4 modes
  all(mode_counts$n == 26),   # Each mode should have 26 rows (13 prov x 2 
                              # genders)
  setequal(
    mode_counts$Mode,         # All modes should be the expected 4 (listed in 
                              # code)
    c("Car, truck or van", "Public transit", "Active transportation", 
      "Other method")),
  nrow(gender_counts) == 2,   # Expected exactly 2 genders
  all(gender_counts$n == 52), # Each gender should have 52 rows (13 prov x 4 
                              # modes)" 
  setequal(gender_counts$Gender, c("Men+", "Women+")), # Gender should be listed
                                                       # as either "Men+" or 
                                                       # "Women+"
  n_distinct(commute_clean$Geography) == 13 # Expected exactly 13 provinces and 
                                            # territories
)
```

# Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
# Beginning with head and tail of data to see the top 6 and bottom 6 values in 
# the data frame

clean_data <- read.csv("Cleaned_Commute.csv")

head(clean_data)
tail(clean_data)
```

```{r}
# Random slice of 6 rows from data frame to view a sample of what variation is 
# in the dataset. Seed used to ensure reproducibility

set.seed(723)

clean_data |>
slice_sample(n = 6)
```

```{r}
# Running glimpse to, once again, verify that structure of clean_data is what 
# is expected so that EDA is done intentionally and accurately (not on data 
# that is incorrectly cleaned or read in)

clean_data |>
  glimpse()
```
```{r}
# Creating a summary table that is grouped by Mode & Gender to create summary 
# statistics that are meaningful and comparable, rather than mixing four 
# different modes of transportation. This creates 8 rows of summary statistics 
# (one for each mode and gender pairing) with minimum, maximum, median, and mean 
# calculated in percentages 

clean_data |>
  group_by(Mode, Gender) |>
  summarise( 
    n = n(),
    national_pct = sum(Count) / sum(Total) * 100, 
    min_pct = min(Percent),
    median_pct = median(Percent), 
    mean_pct = mean(Percent), 
    max_pct = max(Percent), 
    .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
  rename(
    "Mode" = Mode, 
    "Gender" = Gender, 
    "National (%)" = national_pct, 
    "Mean (%)" = mean_pct,
    "Median (%)" = median_pct, 
    "Minimum (%)" = min_pct, 
    "Maximum (%)" = max_pct
  ) |> 
  tt() |> 
  format_tt(j = 3:8, digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  style_tt(j = 1:8, align = "llrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
# Transit share by province, men vs. women
transit_eda <- commute_clean |> 
  filter(Mode == "Public transit")

nrow(transit_eda) # should be 26
```
```{r}
# Plotting transit use percentage points by Geography & Gender to visualize
# potential gendered and/or geographic differences in transit use across Canada.

ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Percent, y = fct_reorder(Geography, Percent), 
                        colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) +
  labs(
    title = "What Does the Distribution of Transit Users Look Like Across 
    Canadian Provinces and Territories?", 
    x = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
```{r}
# Creating a table that illustrates the exact gap between Men+ and Women+ 
# transit use (gap measured in percentage points and calculated as ratio)

gap <- transit_eda |>
  select(Geography, Gender, Percent) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gender, values_from = Percent) |>
  mutate(
    gap_pp = `Women+` - `Men+`,        # difference in percentage points
    ratio  = `Women+` / `Men+`         # how many times higher women's share is
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(gap_pp)) 

gap |>
  tt() |>
  format_tt(j = 4, digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  setNames(c("Province", "Men+", "Women+", "Gap (pp)", "Ratio"))
```

```{r}
# Visualizing gender difference in transit use (Women+ minus Men+) by province 
# to express which provinces/territories have the largest & smallest gender 
# differences in transit use (as well as if there are provinces/territories 
# with inverted gender differences)

gap <- gap |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(gap_pp > 0, "Women+ higher", "Men+ higher"))

ggplot(gap, aes(x = gap_pp, y = fct_reorder(Geography, gap_pp), 
                fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Women+ higher" = "#6CCED9", "Men+ higher" = "#EC9C3E")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Do Women Use Transit More Than Men in 
    Canadian Provinces and Territories?", 
    x = "Gap in percentage points (Women+ minus Men+)",
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```

```{r}
# Creating a list of province/territory abbreviations for following graph's 
# labels (to reduce clutter on graph)

prov_abbr <- c(
  "Newfoundland and Labrador" = "NL", 
  "Prince Edward Island" = "PEI", 
  "Nova Scotia" = "NS", 
  "New Brunswick" = "NB", 
  "Quebec" = "QC", 
  "Ontario" = "ON", 
  "Manitoba" = "MB", 
  "Saskatchewan" = "SK", 
  "Alberta" = "AB", 
  "British Columbia" = "BC", 
  "Yukon" = "YT", 
  "Northwest Territories" = "NWT", 
  "Nunavut" = "NU"
)
```

```{r}
# Plotting each province/territory by transit use percentage and total number of
# commuters (plotting each province/territory twice - one for each gender).

# Logarithmic scale used to account for significant differences between 
# commuter totals in small provinces/territories (such as NU, NWT, and YT) and 
# commuter totals in large provinces (such as ON, BC, and QC) and prevent a
# a large space in the centre of the graph & clustered points close together on 
# the far ends.

ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Total, y = Percent, colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = unname(prov_abbr[Geography])),
                size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) + 
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 12),
    breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 2),
    labels = \(x) paste0(x)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) + 
  labs(
    title = "Does a Province/Territory's Population Impact 
    their Proportion of Transit Users?", 
    x = "Total commuters (log scale)", 
    y = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    colour = "Gender"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
# Reflections on EDA
I am not surprised to see that there are large variations in commuter and 
transit totals between provinces/territories due to population numbers and 
robustness of transit systems between large provinces (such as ON, BC, and QC) 
and small or rural provinces/territories (such as NU, NWT, YT).

Additionally, women use transit more than men in the majority of the 13 
provinces/territories (10 of 13). While the difference between men's and women's 
transit use is only between 0.2-4.6 percentage points (pp), it does point to a 
trend that I would follow and examine further if I were doing statistical 
analysis on this dataset/research question.

What did surprise me is that there are 3 provinces/territories that had an 
inverse relationship between gender and transit use (NWT, NU, and NL). Upon 
first seeing this, I wondered if this could have something to do with northern 
climate/environment and masculinity, but upon thinking through this further, I 
question if this theory would hold considering that Yukon has a positive gender 
gap of 0.7 pp in comparison to Newfoundland & Labrador's (NL) -0.8 pp gap.
